title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 309
paragraphs: Thus it is as regards the fish. For anointing, those of the Egyptians who dwell in the fens use oil from the castor-berry, which oil the Egyptians call kiki, and they do this as follows. They sow along the banks of the rivers and pools these plants, which grow of themselves in wild form in the land of the Hellenes; sown in Egypt, they produce berries in great quantity but of an evil smell. When they have gathered these, some cut them up and press the oil from them; others again roast them first and then boil them down, collecting the oil that runs out. The oil is fat and no less suitable for burning than olive oil, but it gives off a disagreeable smell.
